about: How the synthetic Guarani voice (facebook/mms-tts-grn, tools/make-tts.py) is given the words that are not Guarani spelling: Spanish names, numbers and loans inside Guarani lines. For the synthesis text only: the screens and the manifest keep the course's spelling. The voice reads letters the Guarani way (c before i as «ch» or «k»; a word without a written mark with the stress on its last vowel), so a Spanish word is written here as a Guarani speaker would spell what is said: h for the jota, k for c and qu, s for c and z, and the acute on the stressed vowel when it is not the last. 'words': the course's word in lower case → what the voice is given, and why. 'as_written': the start of names that are Guarani spelling and are said as written, with any suffix (Itauguápe). 'spanish': a line of the Guarani voices made of these words alone is said by the Spanish voice, in the pitch of the speaker whose line it is. A word that is not here and is not Guarani spelling stops tools/make-tts.py, with its key. Every entry was said three times or more and sent through two speech recognisers (sound/VOICE.md, «How the text is prepared»); none was heard by a person.

juan.why: The Spanish jota. After «che réra» the model says the name with an h by itself, but after «mba'éichapa» it came back «joan»; with h it is the same every time.

josé.why: The Spanish jota; the last vowel is stressed without a mark. Came back «josé» from the large recogniser, as the Spanish spelling did.

jose.why: The same name written without its accent.

lucas.why: c before a is k, and the stress is on the u: without the acute, Guarani stress falls on the last vowel. With it the independent recogniser writes «…úkas» in 6 takes of 6; without it, in 1 of 6. The l often comes back as n or nd («nukas»).

lucía.why: c before i is s. As «lucía» it came back «luchía», «lukía»; as «lusía», «lusía» from the large recogniser in 2 takes of 3.

lucia.why: The same name written without its accent.

luis.why: As written; listed because it ends in a consonant. Came back «nuis», «luis», «ndúi»: the l and the last s are weak.

marta.why: The stress is on the first a; the acute keeps it there.

mateo.why: The stress is on the e. Without the acute it came back «mate'o», a break before the o.

nilda.why: The stress is on the i. The cluster ld is not Guarani and stays poor in every spelling («níva», «nírda»).

pedro.why: The stress is on the e. The model knows the name (the large recogniser heard «pedro» both ways); the acute does no harm.

ramona.why: The stress is on the o. With the acute the o is 52 ms longer against the last a than without, and the large recogniser writes «ramóna» or «ramóma» in 6 takes of 6; without it, never.

rosa.why: The stress is on the o. With the acute the recognisers write «rósa» in 8 hearings of 12; without it, in none. The r is the soft Guarani r, not the strong first r of Spanish.

ana.why: The stress is on the first a. With the acute the recognisers write «á…» in 12 hearings of 12; without it, in none.

carlos.why: c before a is k; the stress is on the a. The cluster rl is not Guarani and stays poor («cálos», «cáryos»).

sofía.why: As written: the stress is marked already. The voice has no f: both recognisers heard «sosía» in 3 takes of 3. Listen to it first.

sofia.why: The same name written without its accent.

tomás.why: As written; listed because it ends in a consonant. Came back «tomás» from the large recogniser in 3 takes of 3.

tomas.why: The same name written without its accent.

luque.why: qu is k, and the stress is on the u. As «luque» it came back «nupie», «nuke»; as «lúke», «núke», «lúke».

argentina.why: g before e is the jota: h. The stress is on the i.

argentina-gua.why: The place name with -gua, as one word: h for the jota, no hyphen (the model has a hyphen that makes no sound of its own), and no acute, because -gua takes the stress. Came back «ahentinagua» from both recognisers.

diez.why: z is s. Only for a number inside a Guarani sentence: a line that is nothing but a Spanish number goes to the Spanish voice (see 'spanish'), because the Guarani voice has no d without n and drops a last l: «diez mil» came back garbled («riesmi», «ndiehmi», «liémi») in each of the eight spellings tried.

mil.why: As written; listed because it ends in a consonant. The last l is not said: the two recognisers heard «mi» in 5 hearings of 6, «miĩ» in the other.

veinte.why: The stress is on the e. Came back «véinte» from both recognisers in 6 takes of 6.

doce.why: c before e is s; the stress is on the o. Came back «ndose»: the d comes out as the Guarani nd.
